  anything in experiments/factory/, or experiments/train/forge_train.py except the one filter in E3. Do not run
  make_jobs.py, teacher.py or patterns.py, and do not write anything under results/.

- **§3** `experiments/final/runner_final.py` (arm FT on the same yardstick as the baselines).
- **§3b** the BX finisher (`--arms BX --fill-missing …`), cloud box + cloud grader, exit 3 when incomplete.
- **§6** `deploy/modal_forge.py` + `experiments/final/run_final_session.sh` (deploy, wait ready, cap with reserve,
  trap that always stops the app).
- **§7** `experiments/final/compare.py` (paired bootstrap, bars (a)-(d), refusals).

  experiments/train/forge_train.py's training-data loader only: drop (and count in the log) any record whose `teacher`
  is not `spark` (records without the field are refused unless they come from the factory's train_records.jsonl, which
  only holds Spark PASS answers), and refuse to start if any loaded file came from a run with `--escalate`. teacher.py is
  NOT edited this round (it would change factory_version). Tests for both.
- **E2, compare.py inputs (PLAN.md step 6, lines 81-92):** inputs are FT's run dir, the baseline dirs main-B2BX and
  main-BR, AND the step-6a BX-finisher dir; BX is merged over all 90 answers (no (job, rep) twice; refuse on a
  duplicate); refuse if any (job, rep) of BX is still missing or 6a ended INCOMPLETE; bar (d) uses BX tokens over all
  90 answers; BX wall-clock for "per correct part" = 3,050 s (baseline arm) + 6a's arm wall-clock without the cold
  start; report the 79-answer value next to it (disclosure).
- **N1:** runner_final writes `grader: first-test|factory` into every calls.jsonl record, and the dev summary prints
  the PLAN step-5 gate (dev ≥ 80% at 0.2% → GO, else STOP).
- Grading note: the exam (first-test) uses `checks.score` exactly as the baselines; the factory dev jobs use the factory
  grader (precise volumes, round 1d). Do not mix them.

## Done when
- `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/factory experiments/freecad
  experiments/train experiments/common` passes (259 plus the new tests).
- `runner_final.py --jobs main --out X` with no keys exits 2 with the missing-variable message, no network.
- `forge_train.py smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` still prints CAP REFUSED and exits 2.
- the forge_train loader test shows a non-spark record is dropped and an --escalate run is refused.
Report at the end: files changed, the pytest line, and anything you did not follow.

1|# Training + final exam plan (DRAFT, prepared not run)
2|
3|Status: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-10-29 ~22:30. User: "prepare the training, not run". Nothing here has been paid or run.
4|Order of gates: verifier check of this plan + MUSE_SPEC.md → user's yes to the Muse build → build + tests → verifier
5|→ user's yes (and budget raise) for each paid run step below.
6|
7|## Question (the goal, user 2026-10-29)
8|Is a trained Glimmer 30B, with a short prompt and one try, **as correct as Glimmer + every fair fix (B-max, 95%)**
9|on the 30 held-out CadQuery jobs, and **many times cheaper and faster**, while running on one GPU that a company owns?
10|
11|## Why privately run Glimmer is the comparison, not Spark (verified)
12|- Spark Open is 816B parameters (42B active) and needs ≥ 700 GB GPU memory for NVFP4 (one B200 node; BF16 = 4 nodes
13|  of 8 H200). Source: https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B and
14|  https://huggingface.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open. Glimmer 30B is dense ~29.6B; its 4-bit build is < 20 GB (fits a
15|  24-32 GB GPU). Source: https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.
16|- Fair note (verifier F4): the Spark Open model card also says it is "optimized to run on two Mac Studios with M5
17|  Ultra using MLX". So private Spark is possible, but needs ~700 GB of memory (two top Mac Studios or a B200 node);
18|  Glimmer needs < 20 GB.
19|- decision: the headline compares trained vs untrained Glimmer **on the same A100-80GB**. We never claim "cheaper than
20|  Spark via an API" (it is not: Spark on Baseten ≈ $0.017 per answer, 18 s). Spark appears only as the teacher and in a
21|  "why not run Spark privately" line with the hardware figures above.
22|
23|## Steps (each paid step needs the user's yes; caps are hard stops)
24|| # | Step | Where | Cap | Expected |
25||---|---|---|---|---|
26|| 0 | Muse Code build (MUSE_SPEC.md: cloud CadQuery box, factory, trained arm, compare script, C1 fix) | Meta | — | $2-4 (1-2 rounds + fixes) |
27|| 1 | Comparability check: the cloud box + grader re-run the 270 recorded baseline answers; verdicts must equal the recorded ones | Modal CPU | $0.50 | ~$0.10 |
28|| 2 | Factory pilot: 20 jobs (2 per family), Spark k=1 | Baseten + Modal CPU | $1.00 | ~$0.5 |
29|| 3 | Factory main: ~170 jobs (yield rule in experiments/factory/PLAN.md) | Baseten + Modal CPU | $5.00 (incl. step 2) | ~$4.2 |
30|| 4 | Training: LoRA on H100 + merge | Modal H100 | $4.00 | ~$2-3 |
31|| 5 | Dev check: trained model on the 20 dev jobs, k=3 | Modal A100 | $1.00 | ~$0.5 |
32|| 6a | Finish BX: its 11 missing answers (H12 ×2, H13-H15 ×3), base Glimmer, 12 workers (one wave) | Modal A100 | $1.00 | ~$0.6 (worst ≈ $0.74) |
33|| 6 | Final exam: trained model on the 30 exam jobs, k=3 | Modal A100 | $2.00 | ~$1 |
34|| 7 | (optional, free GPU) offline Mac demo with MLX | Mac + Modal CPU | $0.30 | ~$0 |
35|Total ≈ **$10-14 expected; worst case caps $13.80 + Muse $3-5 = $16.8-18.8** (verifier N2, + step 6a) → Forge ≈ $41-45
36|expected, ≈ $49 worst, of the $50 the user may approve. Within the
37|current $35 only step 0 fits. decision (user, 2026-10-29): budget raised to $50; each paid step still needs the
38|user's yes and the verifier.
39|
40|## Step 1: comparability (why: baselines were graded on the Mac; the trained arm will be graded in the cloud)
41|Re-run the code of the 199 recorded final answers (BR 30, B2 90, BX 79; results/bmax-baseline-2026-10-29) in the
42|cloud box and grade it in the cloud grader, recording both 0.2% and 1e-6. Box and grader pin the Mac's versions:
43|cadquery==2.8.0, cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1. Pass = 0 verdict changes at 0.2%, AND the box's measurements (bbox, volume,
44|solids) equal the recorded ones at print precision (verifier A3: BX's round 2 feeds these measurements back to the
45|model, so a Mac-vs-cloud difference would change BX's conversation). Any change → STOP and explain before step 6 (a grader difference
46|would make the comparison unfair).
47|
48|## Steps 2-3: factory (frozen plan: experiments/factory/PLAN.md, spec experiments/factory/SPEC.md)
49|Changes from this plan: teacher answers run in the cloud box (not the Mac sandbox); `cached_tokens` read from
50|`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (C1, verifier). Before the pilot, Claude does the blind rebuild: one job
51|per family from its text alone through the cloud box, 10/10 PASS at 1e-6.
52|
53|## Step 4: training (pipeline: experiments/train/forge_train.py, built and tested; smoke test passed)
54|- decision: one configuration, chosen before seeing any dev result: epochs 2, LoRA r 16 / alpha 32, lr 1e-4, grad
55|  accumulation 8, max 4,096 tokens per example, short prompt (first-test SYSTEM_PROMPT + job text), loss on the answer
56|  only. Same as the smoke test that passed.
57|- The exam guard runs first (refuses exam look-alikes; aborts if > 5% refused). Its code check now uses the cloud box.
58|- Stop early if peak memory after the first optimizer step > 76 GB (built in).
59|- Log: loss per step, examples dropped for length, tokens learned, minutes, $ (Modal billing before/after).
60|
61|## Step 5: dev check (pre-registered gate before the exam is touched)
62|Trained model on the 20 dev jobs (never trained on), k = 3, strict 1e-6 and 0.2% both reported; decision on 0.2%.
63|- dev ≥ 80% → GO to the final exam.
64|- dev < 80% → STOP. Report it. One retry (epochs 3) only with a new user yes; never touch the exam to decide.
65|
66|## Step 6: final exam (rules pre-registered in experiments/bmax/PLAN.md rule 3, copied here unchanged)
67|Arm FT = the trained model, short prompt, one try, k = 3, 8 workers, alone on an A100-80GB, max_tokens 16,000, same
68|sampling (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64), 0.2% referee for the decision, 1e-6 reported. Paired bootstrap over
69|the 30 jobs, 10,000 resamples, each job's pass rate over its answers:
70|- (a) **as good as B-max**: FT − BX ≥ −5 points AND 95% CI lower bound ≥ −15;
71|- (b) **clearly beats the one-try arm**: 95% CI of FT − B2 entirely above 0;
72|- (c) **about the same cost as B2**: FT tokens per correct part ≤ 1.5 × B2's (≤ 15,993);
73|- (d) **much cheaper than B-max**: FT tokens per correct part ≤ BX ÷ 3 (≤ 7,105), or wall-clock per correct part ≤ BX ÷ 3.
74|  Reported first as wall-clock and $ per correct part, then tokens split into prompt and completion (verifier F2):
75|  B2 = 6,458 prompt + 4,205 completion per correct part, BX = 14,101 + 7,213. Most of the token saving comes from
76|  dropping the 5.7k-token manual (the knowledge moved into the weights); the report says so.
77|- The full claim holds only if all four hold. "Within 5 points" is never called "better". Medium and hard are reported
78|  separately (medium is saturated: B2 100%).
79|- Honest-risk note (from the baseline page): (b) will likely fail on 30 jobs even if training works; then the report
80|  says "as good as B-max, N× cheaper" and states that (b) failed.
81|- **BX's 11 missing answers are run (user decision 2026-10-29: "finish until the 30 jobs").** BX had 0 final answers on
82|  H13, H14, H15 and 1 of 3 on H12 (cap stop in the baseline). Step 6a runs only those 11 (job, rep) pairs with the
83|  frozen BX prompt, settings and loop, on the cloud box, base Glimmer on the same A100-80GB. Then all 30 jobs have 3
84|  BX answers and rule 3's 30-job paired bootstrap applies unchanged. Disclosed: these 11 answers ran on a later day
85|  and were graded in the cloud (step 1 shows the grader gives the same verdicts).
86|  - 12 workers, so all 11 run in one wave (verifier A1: hard BX answers take up to 821 s; 8 workers = 2 waves ≈ $1.31
87|    worst, over the cap). Concurrency differs from the baseline's 8, so the median latency is reported too.
88|  - If 6a stops before 11 final answers exist → STOP and ask the user; compare.py is not run.
89|  - Bar (d) is recomputed over all 90 BX answers, as rule 3 says. The 7,105 above is the 79-answer value; hard answers
90|    average 22,303 tokens against 20,235, so the bar will likely get a little looser for FT. Disclosed in the report
91|    (verifier A2).
92|  - BX wall-clock for "per correct part" = 3,050 s (baseline arm) + 6a's arm wall-clock without the cold start.
93|- Reported per arm: pass rate (all / medium / hard), pass@3, tokens per correct part, seconds per answer (median and
94|  mean), $ per correct part (= arm wall-clock h × $2.50 ÷ PASS), chart accuracy vs $ per correct part.
95|
96|## Step 7: offline demo (other agent's condition 3; only if it takes under ~2 h)
97|hypothesis: download the merged model (~56 GB; 587 GB free) and convert it with `mlx_lm.convert -q` on the Mac, then
98|answer one exam-style job offline. The model only writes text on the Mac; its code is still built in the cloud box
99|(rule: no AI-written code runs on the Mac). Shown as a demo, not scored.
100|
101|## Not in this plan
102|- Thinking jobs without the standard (optional idea): later, only if money is left.
103|- No defence or war examples anywhere (user rule).
104|
105|## Before step 6
106|Check that the merged model's generation_config.json equals the base model's (same sampling defaults). Log the vLLM
107|image digest for every session (base and trained).
108|
109|## Freeze (sha256 recorded here before step 6)
110|runner_final.py, cloud_cq.py, the grader, deploy/modal_forge.py, the merged model's file list, this PLAN.

1|# Muse Code spec: cloud CadQuery box, factory, trained arm, final comparison (DRAFT)

3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29. Needs the verifier's check and the user's yes before Muse Code runs.
4|Plan: experiments/final/PLAN.md. Factory details: experiments/factory/SPEC.md (binding, with the changes in §2 here).
5|
6|## Rules
7|- Work in ~/projects/forge. New files only in experiments/final/, experiments/factory/ and deploy/modal_forge.py; the
8|  one allowed edit outside them is §5 (runner_fc.py cached tokens) and §4's guard hook in experiments/train/forge_train.py.

12|  the grader image.

17|## 1. `experiments/final/cloud_cq.py`: cloud CadQuery box + grader
18|Same design as experiments/freecad/cloud_exec.py and cloud_grade.py (read both):
19|- Box: a fresh Modal Sandbox per answer (block_network=True, no secrets, no volumes, cpu 1, memory 1024-4096 MiB,
20|  90 s box, 60 s run = runner.RUN_TIMEOUT). Image: python:3.12-slim + the libGL apt line + `cadquery==2.8.0 cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1` (the
21|  Mac's versions; the grader pins the same) + a small run script. It holds no references, jobs or expected files.
22|- The run script executes answer.py, takes the `result` variable (same rule as runner.run_code: Workplane → its
23|  solid), and writes the part as **BREP** (exact; not STEP) plus a run-error text if it failed.
24|- Grader: a Modal function (app `forge-cq-grader`, cpu 1) with CadQuery 2.8 and checks.py baked in, plus
25|  /grader/first-test/{jobs.py, expected.json} and /grader/factory/jobs.jsonl. `grade(exam, job_id, brep_bytes)` →
26|  {verdict (0.2%, checks.TOL_DIFF), tight (1e-6), fails, measurements}. For first-test it scores against expected.json
27|  exactly as runner.py does; for factory it builds the job's reference program in the grader and scores both ways.
28|- `--check-refs --exam first-test|factory`: each reference built in the box → BREP → grader must PASS at 1e-6.
29|  Prints `REFS n/n PASS`.
30|- `--regrade <baseline results dir>`: re-run each recorded answer's code (from calls.jsonl) in the box, grade it, and
31|  write regrade.json with old verdict, new verdict (0.2%) and new tight (1e-6), per answer (the 199 final
32|  answers: BR 30, B2 90, BX 79), plus a measure-equality column: box measurements vs the recorded ones at the
33|  recorded print precision; print `MEASURE same=X changed=Y`; print `REGRADE same=X changed=Y`. (PLAN step 1.)
34|- Tests: BREP round trip of a simple part keeps volume and bbox at 1e-9; a fake sandbox returns bytes → grader
35|  verdict path; image file list has no references; regrade counts with fake records.
36|
37|## 2. Factory (experiments/factory/SPEC.md, build it, with these changes)
38|- Teacher answers run in cloud_cq's box and are graded by its grader at 1e-6 (not runner.run_code on the Mac).
39|- Reference programs and the generator's own self-checks (valid solids, wrong variants fail) are trusted generator
40|  code and may run locally in tests.
41|- cached tokens: read `usage["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"]` when present, else `usage["cached_tokens"]`,
42|  else 0. Test with the real Baseten usage shape (numbers illustrative):
43|  `{"prompt_tokens": 8307, "completion_tokens": 3438, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 7552}}`.
44|- `make_jobs.py` also writes the 20 dev jobs as a jobs file usable by §3 (`--jobs-file`).
45|
46|## 3. `experiments/final/runner_final.py`: the trained arm FT on the same yardstick
47|- Import from experiments/first-test/runner.py (frozen, unchanged): SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_messages, build_body,
48|  the code extraction, the summary/statistics helpers. Arm FT = arm A's messages (system + job text, no manual, no
49|  hint) and arm A's body (max_tokens 16000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64), with model "forge".
50|  Test: FT's messages and body equal runner.build_messages("A", …) / build_body(…) except the model name.
51|- Endpoint from env FORGE_URL / FORGE_KEY (missing → exit 2 with the variable name, no network).
52|- `--jobs dry|main` (first-test levels, as runner.py) or `--jobs-file <factory dev file>`; `--k`, `--workers 8`,

54|- Each answer: extract code → cloud box → cloud grader. calls.jsonl per answer (append live under a lock): job, rep,
55|  level, verdict (0.2%), tight (1e-6), fails, usage (prompt, completion, reasoning length), t_call_s, finish_reason.

57|  correct part, seconds per answer (median, mean), arm wall-clock, $ per correct part = wall-clock h × $2.50 ÷ PASS.
58|- Budget guard as runner_fc (money left = cap − GPU time since gpu-start × $2.50/h; stop new calls when ≤ reserve).
59|
60|## 3b. Arm BX on the cloud box, only for missing answers (user: "finish until the 30 jobs")
61|- `runner_final.py --arms BX --fill-missing results/bmax-baseline-2026-10-29/main-B2BX`: run only the (job, rep)
62|  pairs with no BX final record (expected: H12 ×2, H13-H15 ×3 = 11), endpoint GLIMMER_URL/GLIMMER_KEY (base Glimmer).

76|record's code (measurements back from the grader-side measure of the BREP). The local sandbox path is removed for

81|

83|Copy of deploy/modal_glimmer.py's settings (A100-80GB, same vLLM image and flags, max-model-len 32768, max_containers
84|1, 5-min scale-down, secret forge-glimmer) except: app `forge-trained`, model path `/vol/<name>/merged` from the
85|`forge-lora` volume (name from env FORGE_MODEL_NAME, default `final`), served name `forge`.

88|runner_final.py with app forge-trained.
89|
90|## 7. `experiments/final/compare.py`: the pre-registered decision (PLAN step 6)
91|Inputs: FT's run dir and the baseline dirs results/bmax-baseline-2026-10-29/main-B2BX and main-BR. Paired bootstrap

226|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):
227|    """PASS iff every check holds and the mismatch fraction is within tol.
228|
229|    `check_fails`: failed checks at the baseline yardstick (bbox, volume,
230|    ...); `mismatch`: answer-XOR-reference fraction of reference volume
231|    (None when the shape could not be intersected). Returns
232|    (passed, fails).
233|    """
234|    fails = list(check_fails or [])
235|    if mismatch is None:
236|        fails = fails + ["mismatch error"]
237|    elif mismatch > tol:
238|        fails = fails + ["mismatch %.1f%%" % (100.0 * mismatch)]
239|    return (not fails), fails

242|def grade_result(check_fails, mismatch, measurements):
243|    """Grade one imported BREP: verdict at 0.2% + the 1e-6 recording.
244|
245|    Returns {"verdict", "tight", "fails", "fails_tight", "measurements"}.
246|    Pure (no cadquery): the Modal function supplies check_fails and the
247|    mismatch fraction from checks.score; tests pass synthetic values.
248|    """
249|    passed, fails = combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, TOL_VERDICT)
250|    passed_tight, fails_tight = combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch,
251|                                               TOL_TIGHT)
252|    return {
253|        "verdict": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL",
254|        "tight": "PASS" if passed_tight else "FAIL",
255|        "fails": fails,
256|        "fails_tight": fails_tight,
257|        "measurements": measurements,
258|    }

264|def precise_volume(shape):
265|    """BRepGProp volume at eps 1e-9 (factory H1, 2026-10-30).
266|
267|    The default Shape.Volume() is noisy on some factory solids (F5 up
268|    to 6.1e-4, F9 2.7e-6), so text-faithful answers failed 1e-6. Only
269|    the volumes feeding the factory mismatch use this; every other
270|    measurement keeps checks.measure as today.
271|    """
272|    from OCP.BRepGProp import BRepGProp as _BRepGProp
273|    from OCP.GProp import GProp_GProps as _GProp
274|
275|    top = shape.wrapped if hasattr(shape, "wrapped") else shape
276|    props = _GProp()
277|    _BRepGProp.VolumeProperties_s(top, props, PRECISE_VOLUME_EPS)
278|    return props.Mass()

281|def factory_mismatch(answer_shape, ref_shape):
282|    """Answer-XOR-reference fraction with precise volumes (factory H1).
283|
284|    Mirrors checks.mismatch exactly except the three volumes (answer,
285|    reference, intersection) come from precise_volume.
286|    """
287|    import sys as _sys
288|
289|    if FIRST_TEST_DIR not in _sys.path:
290|        _sys.path.insert(0, FIRST_TEST_DIR)
291|    import checks as _checks
292|
293|    a, r = _checks.to_shape(answer_shape), _checks.to_shape(ref_shape)
294|    inter = a.intersect(r)
295|    va, vr, vi = (precise_volume(s) for s in (a, r, inter))
296|    return (va + vr - 2 * vi) / vr

299|def factory_score(answer, reference, expected):
300|    """checks.score for factory answers with a precise mismatch (H1).
301|
302|    Mirrors checks.score line for line except the mismatch fraction
303|    uses factory_mismatch. Tolerance behavior (checks.TOL_DIFF) is
304|    unchanged: 1e-6 tight, 0.2% verdict.
305|    """
306|    import sys as _sys
307|
308|    if FIRST_TEST_DIR not in _sys.path:
309|        _sys.path.insert(0, FIRST_TEST_DIR)
310|    import checks as _checks
311|
312|    m = _checks.measure(answer)
313|    fails = _checks.compare(m, expected)
314|    try:
315|        d = factory_mismatch(answer, reference)
316|    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
317|        d, fails = None, fails + [("mismatch error %r" % (e,))[:120]]
318|    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
319|    if d is not None and d > _checks.TOL_DIFF:
320|        fails.append("mismatch %.1f%%" % (100.0 * d))
321|    return (not fails), fails, m

324|def score_shapes(answer_shape, ref_shape, expected, precise_mismatch=False):
325|    """Score built shapes at both tolerances (needs cadquery + checks).
326|
327|    The reference shapes are trusted code (exam jobs.py, the generator);
328|    only model answers must stay out of this process. Returns the
329|    grade_result dict plus "mismatch". `checks` is imported lazily from
330|    the frozen first-test copy. With precise_mismatch=True (the factory
331|    grader, H1) the mismatch uses precise BRepGProp volumes; the
332|    default False path calls checks.score exactly as before.

334|    import sys as _sys
335|
336|    if FIRST_TEST_DIR not in _sys.path:
337|        _sys.path.insert(0, FIRST_TEST_DIR)
338|    import checks as _checks
339|
340|    old = _checks.TOL_DIFF
341|    try:
342|        _checks.TOL_DIFF = TOL_VERDICT
343|        if precise_mismatch:
344|            passed, fails, m = factory_score(answer_shape, ref_shape,
345|                                             expected)
346|        else:
347|            passed, fails, m = _checks.score(answer_shape, ref_shape,
348|                                             expected)

350|        _checks.TOL_DIFF = TOL_TIGHT
351|        if precise_mismatch:

356|                                                  expected)

360|                                  ("bbox", "volume", "area", "com",
361|                                   "solids", "valid")})

372|def build_reference_shape(source):
373|    """Build a factory reference shape from its program source.
374|
375|    The source is trusted generator code; it assigns `result` (same rule
376|    as answers: Workplane gives its solid). Needs cadquery.
377|    """

382|    result = ns["result"]

386|            return vals[0]
387|        return _cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
388|    if isinstance(result, _cq.Assembly):
389|        return result.toCompound()
390|    return result

194|def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps, startup_s=0, spent_dollars=0.0):
195|    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
196|
197|    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
198|    order. `startup_s` is the Modal startup allowance per function: the
199|    worst-case cost of a step is (startup_s + want) * rate, and that is
200|    what must fit in the money left. `spent_dollars` carries earlier spend
201|    in the same entrypoint run (train -> merge -> serve share one cap).
202|    Returns {name: seconds} plus `_left`. Raises CapExceeded when a step
203|    does not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
204|    """
205|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
206|    out = {}
207|    for name, rate, want in steps:
208|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + want, rate)
209|        if cost > left:
210|            raise CapExceeded(
211|                "step %r wants %ds + %ds startup ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only "
212|                "$%.2f is left of the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
213|                % (name, want, startup_s, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
214|            )
215|        out[name] = want
216|        left -= cost
217|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
218|    return out

221|def split_cap(cap_dollars, spent_dollars=0.0, startup_s=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S):
222|    """Reserve merge + serve first, hand the rest to train.
223|
224|    Merge gets 12 min H100, serve 6 min A100; train gets whatever the cap
225|    still covers (startup included). Refuses (CapExceeded) when train
226|    would get under 15 min. Returns {train, merge, serve, startup_s}.
227|    """
228|    merge_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + MERGE_RESERVE_S, H100_RATE)
229|    serve_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + SERVE_RESERVE_S, A100_RATE)
230|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
231|    if merge_cost + serve_cost > left:
232|        raise CapExceeded(
233|            "cap $%.2f (spent $%.2f) cannot reserve merge $%.2f + serve "
234|            "$%.2f; refusing" % (cap_dollars, spent_dollars or 0.0,
235|                                 merge_cost, serve_cost)
236|        )
237|    train_budget = left - merge_cost - serve_cost
238|    train_s = train_budget * 3600.0 / H100_RATE - startup_s
239|    if train_s < MIN_TRAIN_S:
240|        raise CapExceeded(
241|            "cap $%.2f leaves only %ds for train (under %ds); refusing"
242|            % (cap_dollars, max(0, int(train_s)), MIN_TRAIN_S)
243|        )
244|    return {"train": int(train_s), "merge": MERGE_RESERVE_S,
245|            "serve": SERVE_RESERVE_S, "startup_s": startup_s}

258|def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):
259|    """Pure schedule: MICRO-steps (one example each) vs OPTIMIZER steps.
260|
261|    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
262|    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
263|    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
264|    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
265|    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
266|    """
267|    if grad_accum < 1:
268|        raise ValueError("grad_accum must be >= 1")
269|    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
270|    full = total_micro // grad_accum
271|    groups = [grad_accum] * full
272|    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
273|    if leftover:
274|        groups.append(leftover)
275|    if max_steps is not None:
276|        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]
277|    return {"micro_steps": sum(groups),
278|            "optimizer_steps": len(groups),
279|            "groups": groups}

311|# ------------------------------------------------------------ exam guard
312|# Local guard, run BEFORE any remote call. Text side: difflib ratio after
313|# lowercasing; exact-number ratios >= 0.9 refuse, number-collapsed ratios
314|# >= 0.8 warn. Code side: the exam references are built in-process with
315|# experiments/first-test/jobs.py (trusted code); only the training
316|# record's code runs in cloud_cq's box (never on the Mac), measured
317|# grader-side. bbox + volume are compared first at
318|# 1e-6 and the full score runs only on a match. Refused records are
319|# dropped; the run aborts only when more than 5% are refused. The saved
320|# report holds counts only, never reference values.

322|_NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
323|_NUM_TOKEN = " #NUM "

326|def normalize_exact(text):
327|    """Lowercased text with numbers kept (for the refusal ratio)."""
328|    return (text or "").lower()

331|def normalize_collapsed(text):
332|    """Lowercased text with every number replaced by a placeholder."""
333|    return _NUM_RE.sub(_NUM_TOKEN, (text or "").lower())

336|def text_ratios(text, exam_text):
337|    """(exact_ratio, collapsed_ratio) of a training text vs an exam text."""
338|    exact = difflib.SequenceMatcher(
339|        None, normalize_exact(text), normalize_exact(exam_text)).ratio()
340|    collapsed = difflib.SequenceMatcher(
341|        None, normalize_collapsed(text),
342|        normalize_collapsed(exam_text)).ratio()
343|    return exact, collapsed

346|def check_text_record(text, exam_texts):
347|    """Classify one record's text: ("refuse"|"warn"|"ok", detail dict).
348|
349|    Refuse when the exact-number ratio to any exam text is >= 0.9;
350|    warn (counted, not refused) when a number-collapsed ratio is >= 0.8.
351|    `exam_texts` is injectable so tests can use a fake exam set.
352|    """
353|    best_exact, best_collapsed = 0.0, 0.0
354|    for exam in exam_texts:
355|        exact, collapsed = text_ratios(text, exam)
356|        best_exact = max(best_exact, exact)
357|        best_collapsed = max(best_collapsed, collapsed)
358|    detail = {"exact_ratio": round(best_exact, 4),
359|              "collapsed_ratio": round(best_collapsed, 4)}
360|    if best_exact >= EXAM_REFUSE_RATIO:
361|        return "refuse", detail
362|    if best_collapsed >= EXAM_WARN_RATIO:
363|        return "warn", detail
364|    return "ok", detail

371|            return False

382|    strict pass (prefilter decides); pass the checks.score-based scorer

194|def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps, startup_s=0, spent_dollars=0.0):
195|    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
196|
197|    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
198|    order. `startup_s` is the Modal startup allowance per function: the
199|    worst-case cost of a step is (startup_s + want) * rate, and that is
200|    what must fit in the money left. `spent_dollars` carries earlier spend
201|    in the same entrypoint run (train -> merge -> serve share one cap).
202|    Returns {name: seconds} plus `_left`. Raises CapExceeded when a step
203|    does not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
204|    """
205|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
206|    out = {}
207|    for name, rate, want in steps:
208|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + want, rate)
209|        if cost > left:
210|            raise CapExceeded(
211|                "step %r wants %ds + %ds startup ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only "
212|                "$%.2f is left of the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
213|                % (name, want, startup_s, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
214|            )
215|        out[name] = want
216|        left -= cost
217|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
218|    return out

221|def split_cap(cap_dollars, spent_dollars=0.0, startup_s=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S):
222|    """Reserve merge + serve first, hand the rest to train.
223|
224|    Merge gets 12 min H100, serve 6 min A100; train gets whatever the cap
225|    still covers (startup included). Refuses (CapExceeded) when train
226|    would get under 15 min. Returns {train, merge, serve, startup_s}.
227|    """
228|    merge_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + MERGE_RESERVE_S, H100_RATE)
229|    serve_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + SERVE_RESERVE_S, A100_RATE)
230|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
231|    if merge_cost + serve_cost > left:
232|        raise CapExceeded(
233|            "cap $%.2f (spent $%.2f) cannot reserve merge $%.2f + serve "
234|            "$%.2f; refusing" % (cap_dollars, spent_dollars or 0.0,
235|                                 merge_cost, serve_cost)
236|        )
237|    train_budget = left - merge_cost - serve_cost
238|    train_s = train_budget * 3600.0 / H100_RATE - startup_s
239|    if train_s < MIN_TRAIN_S:
240|        raise CapExceeded(
241|            "cap $%.2f leaves only %ds for train (under %ds); refusing"
242|            % (cap_dollars, max(0, int(train_s)), MIN_TRAIN_S)
243|        )
244|    return {"train": int(train_s), "merge": MERGE_RESERVE_S,
245|            "serve": SERVE_RESERVE_S, "startup_s": startup_s}

258|def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):
259|    """Pure schedule: MICRO-steps (one example each) vs OPTIMIZER steps.
260|
261|    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
262|    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
263|    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
264|    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
265|    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
266|    """
267|    if grad_accum < 1:
268|        raise ValueError("grad_accum must be >= 1")
269|    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
270|    full = total_micro // grad_accum
271|    groups = [grad_accum] * full
272|    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
273|    if leftover:
274|        groups.append(leftover)
275|    if max_steps is not None:
276|        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]
277|    return {"micro_steps": sum(groups),
278|            "optimizer_steps": len(groups),
279|            "groups": groups}

2|
3|Recipe from dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer/vllm (official vLLM image and parsers), in Modal's web-server pattern.
4|Adapted on 2026-10-28 from the earlier HerdShot deploy script, with Forge's own app, secret and volumes, so the two
5|projects never share state.
6|
7|    modal deploy deploy/modal_glimmer.py     # prints the endpoint URL
8|    modal app stop forge-glimmer             # after every session: no idle GPU left running
9|
10|Budget: Forge has $30 max in total (user, 2026-10-28). max_containers=1 and a 5-minute scale-down cap the spend rate.
11|Needs the Modal secret `forge-glimmer` with VLLM_API_KEY (the endpoint rejects calls without it). Glimmer's weights
12|are not gated, so no HF token is needed. Create the secret from envsave (FORGE_GLIMMER_VLLM_API_KEY) and never write
13|the value to a file.
14|"""
15|import subprocess
16|
17|import modal

20|SERVED_NAME = "muse-glimmer"
21|GPU = "A100-80GB"

11|# The old 4-field form "<jobs>:<subdir>:<arms>:<k>" still means first-test.

16|# envsave takes the OPAQUE id, not the name.
17|export BASETEN_KEY=$(envsave get es_LMDrY_C1YRDJYOAGLb2hB1y5WpczSEujtnquV4V5DTzZSMhp)

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""Run one cloud CadQuery answer inside the box (MUSE_SPEC section 1).
3|
4|Invoked in the box as:
5|    <python> run_cq_box.py <scratch-dir>
6|
7|Reads <scratch>/answer.py, executes it with ``__name__ == "__main__"``,
8|requires a variable ``result`` (same rule as runner.run_code: a
9|Workplane gives its solid), exports it to the fixed path
10|<scratch>/answer.brep as **BREP** (exact; not STEP), writes the
11|measurements to the fixed path <scratch>/measure.json, then prints one
12|JSON line ``MEASURE {...}`` and the brep path. The runner reads only the
13|two fixed files and ignores stdout for them.
14|"""
15|
16|import json
17|import os
18|import sys
19|
20|
21|def _to_shape(result, cq):
22|    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
23|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
24|        if len(vals) == 1:
25|            return vals[0]
26|        return cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
27|    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
28|        return result.toCompound()
29|    return result
30|
31|
32|def measure(shape):
33|    """checks.measure-style dict (bbox, volume, area, com, solids, valid)."""
34|    import cadquery as cq
35|
36|    s = _to_shape(shape, cq)
37|    bb = s.BoundingBox()
38|    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
39|    return {
40|        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in
41|                 (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
42|        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
43|        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
44|        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
45|        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
46|        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
47|    }
48|
49|
50|def main(argv):
51|    scratch = os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(argv[1]))
52|    answer_path = os.path.join(scratch, "answer.py")
53|    brep_path = os.path.join(scratch, "answer.brep")
54|    with open(answer_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
55|        src = f.read()
56|    ns = {"__name__": "__main__"}
57|    exec(compile(src, answer_path, "exec"), ns)
58|    if "result" not in ns:
59|        print("ERROR: no variable named 'result'", file=sys.stderr)
60|        return 2
61|    result = ns["result"]

63|    from cadquery import exporters as _ex

72|    print(brep_path, flush=True)

75|

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""Run one cloud CadQuery answer inside the box (MUSE_SPEC section 1).
3|
4|Invoked in the box as:
5|    <python> run_cq_box.py <scratch-dir>
6|
7|Reads <scratch>/answer.py, executes it with ``__name__ == "__main__"``,
8|requires a variable ``result`` (same rule as runner.run_code: a
9|Workplane gives its solid), exports it to the fixed path
10|<scratch>/answer.brep as **BREP** (exact; not STEP), writes the
11|measurements to the fixed path <scratch>/measure.json, then prints one
12|JSON line ``MEASURE {...}`` and the brep path. The runner reads only the
13|two fixed files and ignores stdout for them.
14|"""
15|
16|import json
17|import os
18|import sys
19|
20|
21|def _to_shape(result, cq):
22|    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
23|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
24|        if len(vals) == 1:
25|            return vals[0]
26|        return cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
27|    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
28|        return result.toCompound()
29|    return result
30|
31|
32|def measure(shape):
33|    """checks.measure-style dict (bbox, volume, area, com, solids, valid)."""
34|    import cadquery as cq
35|
36|    s = _to_shape(shape, cq)
37|    bb = s.BoundingBox()
38|    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
39|    return {
40|        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in
41|                 (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
42|        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
43|        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
44|        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
45|        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
46|        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
47|    }
48|
49|
50|def main(argv):
51|    scratch = os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(argv[1]))
52|    answer_path = os.path.join(scratch, "answer.py")
53|    brep_path = os.path.join(scratch, "answer.brep")
54|    with open(answer_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
55|        src = f.read()
56|    ns = {"__name__": "__main__"}
57|    exec(compile(src, answer_path, "exec"), ns)
58|    if "result" not in ns:
59|        print("ERROR: no variable named 'result'", file=sys.stderr)
60|        return 2
61|    result = ns["result"]
62|    import cadquery as cq
63|    from cadquery import exporters as _ex
64|
65|    shape = _to_shape(result, cq)
66|    m = measure(shape)
67|    _ex.export(shape, brep_path, exportType="BREP")
68|    with open(os.path.join(scratch, "measure.json"), "w",
69|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
70|        json.dump(m, f)
71|    print("MEASURE " + json.dumps(m), flush=True)
72|    print(brep_path, flush=True)
73|    return 0
74|
75|
76|if __name__ == "__main__":
77|    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

1281|def _rec_calls_tokens_latency(rec):
1282|    """(model calls, total tokens, summed model-call latency) for one final
1283|    record. Latency is model call time only, the same definition for every
1284|    arm (FIX_SPEC item 6)."""
1285|    if "model_calls" in rec:
1286|        tokens = (rec.get("prompt_tokens_total", 0) or 0) + \
1287|            (rec.get("completion_tokens_total", 0) or 0)
1288|        return (rec.get("model_calls", 1) or 0, tokens,
1289|                rec.get("latency_total", rec.get("latency", 0) or 0) or 0)
1290|    prompt_n, completion_n = _usage_pair(rec.get("usage"))
1291|    latency = rec.get("latency", None)
1292|    if latency is None:
1293|        latency = rec.get("seconds", 0) or 0
1294|    return 1, prompt_n + completion_n, latency or 0

1297|def _rec_token_split(rec):
1298|    """(input tokens, output tokens) for one final record."""
1299|    if "prompt_tokens_total" in rec or "completion_tokens_total" in rec:
1300|        try:
1301|            prompt = int(rec.get("prompt_tokens_total", 0) or 0)
1302|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
1303|            prompt = 0
1304|        try:
1305|            completion = int(rec.get("completion_tokens_total", 0) or 0)
1306|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
1307|            completion = 0
1308|        return prompt, completion
1309|    return _usage_pair(rec.get("usage"))

1312|def arm_stats(records, arm, extra=False, k=1, wall_seconds=None):
1313|    arm_recs = [r for r in records if r.get("arm") == arm]
1314|    n_pass = sum(1 for r in arm_recs if r.get("outcome") == "PASS")
1315|    n_fail = sum(1 for r in arm_recs if r.get("outcome") == "FAIL")
1316|    n_inv = sum(1 for r in arm_recs if r.get("outcome") == "INVALID")
1317|    scored = n_pass + n_fail
1318|    by_job = {}
1319|    for r in arm_recs:
1320|        by_job.setdefault(r.get("job"), []).append(r)
1321|    n_jobs = len(by_job)
1322|    jobs_with_pass = sum(
1323|        1 for rs in by_job.values()
1324|        if any(x.get("outcome") == "PASS" for x in rs)
1325|    )
1326|    splits = [_rec_token_split(r) for r in arm_recs]
1327|    sum_in = sum(p for p, _ in splits)
1328|    sum_out = sum(c for _, c in splits)
1329|    sum_tokens = sum_in + sum_out
1330|    sum_calls = sum(_rec_calls_tokens_latency(r)[0] for r in arm_recs)
1331|    stats = {
1332|        "n": len(arm_recs),
1333|        "PASS": n_pass,
1334|        "FAIL": n_fail,
1335|        "INVALID": n_inv,
1336|        "pass_rate": (n_pass / scored) if scored else None,
1337|        "invalid_rate": (n_inv / len(arm_recs)) if arm_recs else None,
1338|        # FIX_SPEC items 6-7: per-arm cost/usage numbers over all answers.
1339|        "calls": sum_calls,
1340|        "input_tokens": sum_in,
1341|        "output_tokens": sum_out,
1342|        "total_tokens": sum_tokens,
1343|        "k": k,
1344|        "pass_at_k": (jobs_with_pass / n_jobs) if n_jobs else None,
1345|    }
1346|    if wall_seconds is not None:
1347|        stats["wall_seconds"] = wall_seconds
1348|        stats["dollars_per_pass"] = (
1349|            (wall_seconds / 3600.0 * GPU_DOLLARS_PER_HOUR / n_pass)
1350|            if n_pass else None
1351|        )
1352|    if extra:
1353|        totals = [_rec_calls_tokens_latency(r) for r in arm_recs]
1354|        n = len(arm_recs)
1355|        sum_latency = sum(s for _, _, s in totals)
1356|        denom = n_jobs or n
1357|        stats.update({
1358|            "mean_calls_per_job": (sum_calls / denom) if denom else None,
1359|            "mean_tokens_per_job": (sum_tokens / denom) if denom else None,
1360|            "mean_latency_per_job": (sum_latency / denom) if denom else None,
1361|            "tokens_per_pass": (sum_tokens / n_pass) if n_pass else None,
1362|            "latency_per_pass": (sum_latency / n_pass) if n_pass else None,
1363|        })
1364|    return stats

1367|def compute_decision(rate_b, rate_c, invalid_rates):
1368|    """PLAN.md section 7 from the numbers. Returns (decision, run_valid).
1369|
1370|    Rates are compared in whole percentage points (round(rate*100)).
1371|    Rules apply in order; the first match wins. run_valid is False
1372|    ("run not valid") if INVALID > 5% in any arm.
1373|    """
1374|    run_valid = all(
1375|        (r is None or r <= 0.05) for r in (invalid_rates or {}).values()
1376|    )
1377|    if rate_b is None or rate_c is None:
1378|        decision = "grey zone (too few scored calls)"
1379|    else:
1380|        b_pts = round(rate_b * 100)
1381|        c_pts = round(rate_c * 100)
1382|        gap = c_pts - b_pts
1383|        if b_pts >= 80:
1384|            decision = "STOP (manual is enough)"
1385|        elif c_pts < 20:
1386|            decision = "Spark can't teach"
1387|        elif b_pts <= 60 and c_pts >= 30 and gap >= 25:
1388|            decision = "GO to training"
1389|        else:
1390|            decision = "grey zone"
1391|    if not run_valid:
1392|        decision = "run not valid (INVALID > 5% in an arm); " + decision
1393|    return decision, run_valid

1399|                  arm_timing=None, workers=None):
1400|    arm_timing = arm_timing or {}

1403|    }

1405|        arm: arm_stats(records, arm, extra=True, k=k,
1406|                       wall_seconds=wall[arm])

1409|    levels = sorted({r.get("level") for r in records if r.get("level")})

1416|    cost_c = sum(cost_c_of_usage(u) for u in c_usages)
1417|    gpu_elapsed = gpu_elapsed_s if gpu_elapsed_s is not None else elapsed_s

1426|    costs.update({

1437|    }

1448|        decision = "decision: see experiments/bmax/PLAN.md"
1449|    table = {}

1471|        "gpu_elapsed_seconds": round(gpu_elapsed, 3),

def build_summary(records, ids, spent, spent_w, budget_stopped):
    """Pass rate per family, tokens, cost, the Wonder share."""
    by_family = {}
    for rec in records:
        by_family.setdefault(rec["family"], []).append(rec)
    families = {}
    for fam, recs in sorted(by_family.items()):
        passed = sum(1 for r in recs if r["verdict"] == "PASS")
        families[str(fam)] = {
            "n_calls": len(recs),
            "n_pass": passed,
            "pass_rate": round(passed / len(recs), 4) if recs else 0.0,
        }
    prompt = sum((r.get("usage") or {}).get("prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
                 for r in records)
    completion = sum(
        (r.get("usage") or {}).get("completion_tokens", 0) or 0
        for r in records)
    cached = sum(r.get("cached_tokens", 0) or 0 for r in records)
    n_pass = sum(1 for r in records if r["verdict"] == "PASS")
    kept = {r["id"] for r in records if r["verdict"] == "PASS"}
    wonder_kept = sum(1 for r in build_train_records_from(
        records) if r.get("teacher") == "wonder")
    return {
        "factory_version": FACTORY_VERSION,
        "n_ids": len(ids),
        "n_calls": len(records),
        "n_pass": n_pass,
        "n_kept_ids": len(kept),
        "families": families,
        "prompt_tokens": prompt,
        "completion_tokens": completion,
        "cached_tokens": cached,
        "cost_dollars": round(spent, 4),
        "cost_w_dollars": round(spent_w, 4),
        "wonder_share": (round(wonder_kept / len(kept), 4)
                         if kept else 0.0),
        "budget_stopped": budget_stopped,
    }


def build_train_records_from(records):
    """First PASS per id (the kept answers), with their teacher tag."""
    best = {}
    for rec in records:
        if rec["verdict"] != "PASS" or rec["id"] in best:
            continue
        best[rec["id"]] = rec
    return [best[i] for i in sorted(best)]


def build_train_records(records, jobs_by_id):
    """train_records.jsonl = {"id", "text", "code"} for the first PASS
    at 1e-6 of each id (the teacher's extracted code, not the
    reference)."""
    out = []
    for rec in build_train_records_from(records):
        job = jobs_by_id[rec["id"]]
        out.append({"id": rec["id"], "text": job["text"],
                    "code": rec["code"]})
    return out

def build_summary(records, ids, spent, spent_w, budget_stopped):
    """Pass rate per family, tokens, cost, the Wonder share."""
    by_family = {}
    for rec in records:
        by_family.setdefault(rec["family"], []).append(rec)
    families = {}
    for fam, recs in sorted(by_family.items()):
        passed = sum(1 for r in recs if r["verdict"] == "PASS")
        families[str(fam)] = {
            "n_calls": len(recs),
            "n_pass": passed,
            "pass_rate": round(passed / len(recs), 4) if recs else 0.0,
        }
    prompt = sum((r.get("usage") or {}).get("prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
                 for r in records)
    completion = sum(
        (r.get("usage") or {}).get("completion_tokens", 0) or 0
        for r in records)
    cached = sum(r.get("cached_tokens", 0) or 0 for r in records)
    n_pass = sum(1 for r in records if r["verdict"] == "PASS")
    kept = {r["id"] for r in records if r["verdict"] == "PASS"}
    wonder_kept = sum(1 for r in build_train_records_from(
        records) if r.get("teacher") == "wonder")
    return {
        "factory_version": FACTORY_VERSION,
        "n_ids": len(ids),
        "n_calls": len(records),
        "n_pass": n_pass,
        "n_kept_ids": len(kept),
        "families": families,
        "prompt_tokens": prompt,
        "completion_tokens": completion,
        "cached_tokens": cached,
        "cost_dollars": round(spent, 4),
        "cost_w_dollars": round(spent_w, 4),
        "wonder_share": (round(wonder_kept / len(kept), 4)
                         if kept else 0.0),
        "budget_stopped": budget_stopped,
    }


def build_train_records_from(records):
    """First PASS per id (the kept answers), with their teacher tag."""
    best = {}
    for rec in records:
        if rec["verdict"] != "PASS" or rec["id"] in best:
            continue
        best[rec["id"]] = rec
    return [best[i] for i in sorted(best)]


def build_train_records(records, jobs_by_id):
    """train_records.jsonl = {"id", "text", "code"} for the first PASS
    at 1e-6 of each id (the teacher's extracted code, not the
    reference)."""
    out = []
    for rec in build_train_records_from(records):
        job = jobs_by_id[rec["id"]]
        out.append({"id": rec["id"], "text": job["text"],
                    "code": rec["code"]})
    return out

383|def test_default_box_measure_runs_inside_cloud_cq_app(monkeypatch):
384|    """F1: the exam guard's measure call runs inside cloud_cq._app.run()
385|    (forge_train's own app.run is a different App). A fake app carries
386|    an "entered" flag; the real-path measure call outside the context
387|    fails like Modal's "Function has not been hydrated"."""
388|    import types

390|    state = {"entered": False, "outputs": 0, "runs": 0,
391|             "forge_runs": 0}
392|
393|    class _Ctx:
394|        def __init__(self, flag):
395|            self._flag = flag
396|
397|        def __enter__(self):
398|            self._flag[0] = True
399|
400|        def __exit__(self, *args):
401|            self._flag[0] = False
402|            return False
403|
404|    entered = [False]
405|
406|    class _Modal:
407|        @staticmethod
408|        def enable_output():
409|            state["outputs"] += 1
410|            return _Ctx([False])
411|
412|    class _CloudApp:
413|        def run(self):
414|            state["runs"] += 1
415|            return _Ctx(entered)
416|
417|    class _Measure:
418|        def remote(self, brep_bytes):
419|            if not entered[0]:
420|                raise RuntimeError("Function has not been hydrated")
421|            return {"volume": 1.0, "brep_len": len(brep_bytes)}
422|
423|    fake_cq = types.SimpleNamespace(modal=_Modal(), _app=_CloudApp(),
424|                                    measure_brep=_Measure())
425|    monkeypatch.setattr(forge_train, "_final_cq", lambda: fake_cq)
426|    # Outside the context the real path fails, like unhydrated Modal.
427|    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="has not been hydrated"):
428|        fake_cq.measure_brep.remote(b"B")

+        else:

+                    tight = "FAIL"
+                    run_error = last_error or "code error"
+                    last_code = last_code or ""
+                else:

+                        tight = "FAIL"
+                    if passed:
+                        outcome, run_error = "PASS", None
+                    else:
+                        outcome, run_error = "FAIL", last_error
+                    last_code = best[0]
+    seconds = time.monotonic() - t0
+    end = runner.utcnow_iso()
+    run_error = runner.scrub(run_error, secrets)
+    if run_error and len(run_error) > runner.RUN_ERROR_TAIL:
+        run_error = run_error[-runner.RUN_ERROR_TAIL:]
+    prompt_total = sum(r["prompt_tokens"] for r in rounds)
+    completion_total = sum(r["completion_tokens"] for r in rounds)
+    latency_total = round(sum(r["latency"] for r in rounds), 3)
+    reasoning_total = sum(r["reasoning_len"] for r in rounds)
+    for rnd in rounds:

+    return {
+        "job": job["id"],
+        "rep": rep,
+        "sample": rep,
+        "level": job.get("level"),
+        "arm": BX_ARM,
+        "grader": exam,
+        "model": model,
+        "start": start,
+        "start_time": start,
+        "end": end,
+        "end_time": end,
+        "seconds": round(seconds, 3),
+        "finish_reason": finish_reason,
+        "usage": usage,
+        "content": content,
+        "reasoning_len": reasoning_total,
+        "reasoning_length": reasoning_total,
+        "code": last_code,
+        "extracted_code": last_code,
+        "verdict": outcome,
+        "tight": tight if tight is not None else outcome,
+        "outcome": outcome,
+        "fails": fails or [],
+        "fails_tight": (fails_tight if "fails_tight" in dir() else None)
+        or (fails or []),
+        "failed_checks": fails or [],
+        "measurements": measurements,
+        "run_error": run_error,
+        "round": len(rounds),
+        "bx_final": True,
+        "model_calls": len(rounds),
+        "prompt_tokens_total": prompt_total,
+        "completion_tokens_total": completion_total,
+        "latency_total": latency_total,
+        "bx_rounds": rounds,
+    }

+    baseline arm_timing entry."""
+    if summary.get("wall_seconds") is not None:
+        try:
+            return float(summary["wall_seconds"])
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            pass
+    timing = (summary.get("arm_timing") or {}).get(arm or "")
+    try:
+        return float((timing or {}).get("seconds"))
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):

+    return None

+# ------------------------------------------------------- paired bootstrap
+
+
+def bootstrap_ci(x_rates, y_rates, jobs, n=BOOTSTRAP_N, seed=BOOTSTRAP_SEED):
+    """Paired bootstrap of mean(x - y) over jobs, in percentage points.
+
+    Returns (est, lo, hi): the plain mean difference and the 95% CI
+    (2.5/97.5 percentiles of n resamples with replacement).
+    """
+    est = sum(x_rates[j] - y_rates[j] for j in jobs) / len(jobs)
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    diffs = []
+    for _ in range(n):
+        s = 0.0
+        for _ in jobs:
+            j = jobs[rng.randrange(len(jobs))]
+            s += x_rates[j] - y_rates[j]
+        diffs.append(s / len(jobs))
+    diffs.sort()
+    return (est * 100.0, diffs[int(0.025 * n)] * 100.0,
+            diffs[int(0.975 * n)] * 100.0)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------- bars
+
+
+def check_a(est_pts, lo_pts):
+    """(a) as good as B-max: est >= -5 points AND CI lower >= -15."""
+    return est_pts >= -5.0 and lo_pts >= -15.0
+
+
+def check_b(lo_pts, _hi_pts):
+    """(b) clearly beats the one-try arm: CI entirely above 0."""
+    return lo_pts > 0.0
+
+
+def check_c(ft_tpc, b2_tpc):
+    """(c) about the same cost as B2: FT <= 1.5 x B2 tokens/correct."""
+    return ft_tpc <= 1.5 * b2_tpc
+
+
+def check_d(ft_tpc, bx_tpc, ft_wpc, bx_wpc):
+    """(d) much cheaper than B-max: tokens <= BX/3 OR wall <= BX/3."""
+    return ft_tpc <= bx_tpc / 3.0 or ft_wpc <= bx_wpc / 3.0
+
+
+def tokens_per_correct(finals):
+    """(total, prompt, completion, n_pass, per_correct) over finals."""
+    splits = [split_tokens(r) for r in finals]
+    total = sum(p + c for p, c in splits)
+    prompt = sum(p for p, _ in splits)
+    completion = sum(c for _, c in splits)
+    n_pass = sum(1 for r in finals if is_pass(r))
+    per = (total / n_pass) if n_pass else None
+    return total, prompt, completion, n_pass, per

+
+def dollars_per_correct(wall_s, n_pass):
+    """$ per correct part = wall-clock h x $2.50 / PASS."""
+    if wall_s is None or not n_pass:
+        return None
+    return wall_s / 3600.0 * GPU_DOLLARS_PER_HOUR / n_pass
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------- decision

Done. All round-2 builds are in place and verified.

Files changed (nothing committed):
- [runner_final.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/final/runner_final.py) (new, §3+§3b+N1): arm FT = arm-A messages/body with model `forge`; FT one-shot loop (box → grader); BX cloud loop mirroring frozen `do_bx_call`; `--fill-missing` (workers default 12, exit 3 + `INCOMPLETE: ask the user`); every record carries `grader: first-test|factory`; dev runs print the PLAN step-5 gate; vLLM digest in every summary.
- [test_runner_final.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/final/test_runner_final.py) (new, 14 tests): FT≡arm-A-except-model, BX message-list equality vs frozen loop with real scored shapes, fill-missing/INCOMPLETE, no-keys exit 2, §6 static checks.
- [modal_forge.py](~/projects/forge/deploy/modal_forge.py) (new, §6) + [run_final_session.sh](~/projects/forge/experiments/final/run_final_session.sh) (new, §6): dev pilot + GO/STOP, cap with reserve, trap stops `forge-trained`.
- [compare.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/final/compare.py) (new, §7+E2) + [test_compare.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/final/test_compare.py) (new, 10 tests): 4-input merge, duplicate/missing/INCOMPLETE refusals (exit 2), bootstrap bars at exact boundaries, 79-answer disclosure, BX wall = 3,050 s + 6a sans cold start.
- `experiments/train/forge_train.py` (E3 filter only) + `test_forge_train.py` (3 new tests; 1 existing loader test updated to the new contract).

Verification observed:
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/factory experiments/freecad experiments/train experiments/common` → **284 passed, 2 skipped**.
- `runner_final.py --jobs main --out X` with no keys → exit 2, `missing environment variables: FORGE_URL, FORGE_KEY`, no network.
- `forge_train.py smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` → `CAP REFUSED`, exit 2.
- Loader tests show `dropped_non_spark=2` and the `--escalate` ValueError.

Two deviations to know: (1) the pre-existing loader test asserted teacher-less records load — updated to the E3 contract (smoke examples now load as `[]`; tagging them `spark` would fabricate provenance, so with an adequate cap `run_smoke` would train on zero records — needs a follow-up decision); (2) `compare.py` also refuses when FT lacks a job or no arm has a PASS (needed for the bootstrap/denominators), and exits 1 when bars compute but the claim fails. Live-factory files under `results/` were not touched; scratch checks stayed in `/tmp`.
